chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa al-Absi from Sufyan al-Thawri from Jabir al-Ju'fi from Suwayd ibn Ghaflah said:

Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was asked about the inheritance of a daughter, a wife, and collateral freedmen (mawali). He gave the wife one-eighth, and whatever remained he returned to the daughter, and he gave the mawali nothing.

key_terms.مَوَالِي: Collateral freedmen (clients) in Islamic inheritance law

ai.seo_question: What is the share of mawali in inheritance when competing with a daughter and a wife?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the early juristic application of the principle that *mawali* (collateral freedmen) are excluded from inheritance when competing with direct descendants like a daughter. It highlights the specific allocation where the wife receives her fixed one-eighth share, while the daughter inherits the remainder, reflecting the Shia interpretation of kinship-based distribution. This ruling underscores the distinct status of *mawali* in Shia fiqh compared to other schools, particularly in the absence of closer male agnates.
